items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: That was with Wild Bill -- Wild Bill Davison... I got to know him backwards... we had Wild Bill Davison on trumpet... I will be in concert with him

ctx.x: This is tape four of the Cliff Leeman story, and now Cliff Leeman will continue with his Condon story.

To get back to the Condon band, when I went in with Eddie in '51, that band was the most charging band, the most exciting -- I don't believe they ever had a bad night. I can't remember a bad night there. That was with Wild Bill -- Wild Bill Davison, Edmund Hall, Cutty Cutshall, Schroeder Gene Shrader -- Shrader Shroder -- take your pick.

I got Walter Page, I recommended Walter Page for the job, and Ralph Sutton, Lou McGerrity, and -- in those days, the place was jammed. I've seen them hang from the -- there was a railing around the top there, there was an upper part, and they'd come down from West Point, the Army-Navy games and so forth. And we played with that band, all the traditional Dixieland songs, because they were requested. They were references -- it was a Dixie style orchestra, which it was not. With Wild Bill and Eddie, and the manner…

items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: Bill and I are the only two people alive out of that one... we made a beautiful thing together. We made two albums for Columbia... Jammin' at Condon's and East Coast West Coast Jazz.

ctx.x: So he says, "Jonny Hodges, I'd love to have" -- he said -- "do you suppose he'd do that?" And I said I didn't know, that he'd have to call him. And Ben, my whole life with Ben was just starting then, you know, I was around all the time.
Did you recommend Bill? Were you the one who recommended Bill?
I recommended Ben, and he got Johnny Hodges, and when I came in for the record date, I was surprised that he got what's his name on trombone.

items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: ever since my first years with Wild Bill Davison... We also played Geneva and Zurich... the group the first two years was...

ctx.x: Now I'd like to get to Wild Bill -- Wild Bill

Davi son, and I'm trying to get to these people one by one to keep in context with my career, but we don't have time, as I have said several times before, to get into the many jobs that we've done together.

So I'll skip over lightly on some of the things the first London years over the years, ever since my first years with Wild Bill Davison -- in 1976, he was instrumental in bringing me to the Swiss International Jazz Festival held in Bern, Switzerland. We also played Geneva and Zurich, Germany, the group the first two years was Ed Hubble on trombone, Peanuts Hucko on clarinet, Bob Wilbur on clarinet and there goes my mental block -- on soprano saxophone, Bob Wilbur Ralph Sutton on piano and with the Swiss bassist.

items.title: 63519_Wild Bill Davison oral history interview
items.q: I think the longest time band was probably Edmond Hall and Cutty Cutshall, and Schroeder and Cliff Leeman... I got hold of Cliff Leeman and I got hold of the piano player, you know, Ralph Sutton and we lined the whole thing up

ctx.x: Weren't you considered "the" really basic band? The longest time band--

Well, I think the longest time band was probably Edmond Hall and Cutty Cutshall, and Schroeder and Cliff Leeman and we had drums changed all the time. The changes would be between George Wettling and Cliff Leeman and we had several bass players - changes of bass players in there. And, I think Peanuts and Pee Wee Russell - we had those clarinets - changing from time to time.
